[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Enterprises adopting multiple AI coding assistants (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex) maintain parallel construct catalogs — Commands alongside Prompts, CLAUDE.md alongside copilot-instructions.md, Claude rules alongside Copilot instructions with `applyTo`. Without a synchronization mechanism, these parallel catalogs drift apart over time: behavioral directives conflict, new Commands lack Prompt equivalents, and instruction files convey divergent conventions. This drift causes developers to receive inconsistent guidance depending on which AI assistant they use, undermining the purpose of enterprise-wide standards.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Cross-Tool Construct Synchronization Pattern establishes a **single-source-of-truth model** with **derived artifacts** and **automated parity verification**. One construct catalog is designated as the source; the other is derived through a defined synchronization process. Parity is verified through CI checks that detect drift between source and derived catalogs. The pattern covers three synchronization tiers: Workflows (Commands ↔ Prompts), Instructions (CLAUDE.md ↔ copilot-instructions.md), and Rules (Claude rules ↔ Copilot applyTo instructions).
page_texts.6:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- When a repository supports multiple AI coding assistants simultaneously
- When behavioral consistency across assistants is a governance requirement
- When teams report receiving conflicting guidance from different AI assistants
- When the construct catalog grows beyond 10 items and manual synchronization becomes error-prone
page_texts.7:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

- **Platform Engineers** maintaining AI coding assistant configurations
- **Developers** authoring new constructs that must exist in both tool ecosystems
- **Architects** governing cross-tool behavioral consistency
page_texts.9:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#forces]

### Forces

1. **Multi-tool adoption** — The enterprise has standardized on multiple AI coding assistants to leverage each tool's strengths, but this creates parallel configuration surfaces.
2. **Independent evolution** — Commands and Prompts evolve independently as different team members author in their preferred tool.
3. **Semantic divergence** — The same concept (e.g., "lint the project") may be expressed differently across tools, causing subtle behavioral inconsistencies.
4. **Scale** — As construct catalogs grow (the bootstrap repository has 47 Commands and 62 Prompts), manual synchronization becomes unsustainable.
5. **Governance overhead** — Without automation, reviewers must manually verify parity during every PR that touches AI configurations.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#problem-consequences-without-this-pattern]

### Problem Consequences (Without This Pattern)

- Developers receive inconsistent guidance depending on which AI assistant they use
- New constructs are authored in one tool and forgotten in the other
- Instruction files drift: CLAUDE.md says one thing, copilot-instructions.md says another
- Architecture reviews cannot efficiently verify cross-tool consistency
- Enterprise standards enforcement is undermined by behavioral divergence
page_texts.12:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#solution-structure]

### Solution Structure

The pattern defines three components:
page_texts.13:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#1-source-of-truth-designation]

#### 1. Source of Truth Designation

Each construct tier designates one tool's catalog as the **source** and the other as **derived**:

| Construct Tier | Source of Truth | Derived Artifact | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skills | `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` | `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` (discovery mirror — delegates to canonical path) | Claude Code reads canonical path directly; Copilot/gh-aw discovers via `.github/skills/` pointer |
| Workflows | `.claude/commands/*.md` | `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md` | Commands are structurally simpler; Prompts add frontmatter |
| Instructions | `CLAUDE.md` | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Claude's richer section model is a superset |
| Rules | `.claude/rules/*.md` | `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` | Claude rules have explicit `paths:` frontmatter |

> **Note**: The source-of-truth designation is a convention, not a technical constraint. Teams MAY designate a different source if their workflow favors it, provided the designation is documented and consistent.
page_texts.14:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#2-synchronization-process]

#### 2. Synchronization Process

```
Source Construct Modified
        │
        ▼
Author creates/updates derived construct
        │
        ▼
Structural adaptation applied:
  - Commands → Prompts: Add YAML frontmatter (mode, description, tools)
  - CLAUDE.md → copilot-instructions.md: Reformat sections to Copilot conventions
  - Claude rules → Copilot instructions: Convert paths: YAML list to applyTo: comma-separated string
        │
        ▼
Semantic equivalence verified (behavioral directives match)
        │
        ▼
Both artifacts committed in the same PR
```
page_texts.15:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#3-parity-verification]

#### 3. Parity Verification

Automated CI checks verify synchronization:

- **Catalog count check** — Number of Commands ≈ number of Prompts (within a defined tolerance)
- **Name mapping check** — Every Command file has a corresponding Prompt file (kebab-case name match)
- **Content drift detection** — Instruction files are compared for semantic divergence (manual review triggered when diff exceeds threshold)
- **Staleness detection** — Derived artifacts with older modification timestamps than their source are flagged
page_texts.17:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#commands--prompts]

#### Commands → Prompts

| Command Element | Prompt Equivalent |
|---|---|
| First line (intent statement) | `description:` frontmatter field |
| `$ARGUMENTS` references | Prompt parameter handling |
| Numbered steps | Instruction body (same format) |
| Skill path references | Skill path references (unchanged) |
| N/A | `mode:` field (must be determined from content) |
| N/A | `tools:` field (must be determined from steps) |
| Command that is a thin entry point wrapping one AI-native step (e.g., a router that invokes one skill based on content analysis) | Prompt that uses Copilot's inclusion/attachment mechanism for that step — composition-by-inclusion, not chained execution. Behavioral equivalence is the parity target; mechanical equivalence is not required. |

> **Cross-tool composition note:** Claude Code commands MAY reference other commands via slash-form per [GUID-TECH-IMPL-006](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md) §Command Invocation Boundary and STD-TEC-AI-004 MR-9. GitHub Copilot Prompts compose by file inclusion — a structurally different mechanism. When mapping a Claude Code command that delegates to another command, the Copilot mirror uses inclusion rather than attempting to replicate the slash-form invocation. Parity verification for these pairs should assess semantic equivalence of outputs, not structural identity of composition steps.
page_texts.18:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#claudemd--copilot-instructionsmd]

#### CLAUDE.md → copilot-instructions.md

| CLAUDE.md Section | copilot-instructions.md Equivalent |
|---|---|
| Project Overview | Project Overview (same) |
| Setup | Setup (same) |
| Structure | Structure (same) |
| Skill Invocation Transparency | (Copilot-specific: reference in Role Guidance) |
| Role-Specific Guidance | Role-Specific Guidance (same) |
| Conventions | Conventions (same) |
| Do NOT | Do NOT (same) |
page_texts.19:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#claude-rules--copilot-instructions]

#### Claude Rules → Copilot Instructions

| Claude Rule Element | Copilot Instruction Equivalent |
|---|---|
| `paths:` frontmatter (YAML list) | `applyTo:` frontmatter (comma-separated string) |
| `description:` frontmatter | `description:` frontmatter (same) |
| Rule body | Instruction body (same content) |
page_texts.20:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#consequences]

### Consequences

**Benefits:**

- Developers receive consistent guidance regardless of AI assistant choice
- New constructs are created in pairs, preventing orphaned configurations
- Automated verification catches drift before it reaches production
- Architecture reviews focus on content quality rather than mechanical parity checks

**Liabilities:**

- Adds synchronization overhead to every construct change
- Requires CI infrastructure for parity checks
- Source-of-truth designation may create friction if teams prefer the derived tool
- Structural mapping is not always 1:1 — edge cases require manual judgment. A named recurring edge case: Claude Code commands constrained to single-dispatch routing (thin entry points) map to Copilot Prompts that use composition-by-inclusion rather than direct command equivalents (see Commands → Prompts table note above)
page_texts.22:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#phase-1-establish-source-of-truth]

### Phase 1: Establish Source of Truth

1. Audit existing construct catalogs across both tools.
2. Designate the source of truth for each tier (or accept the defaults above).
3. Document the designation in the repository's `AGENTS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
page_texts.23:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#phase-2-initial-synchronization]

### Phase 2: Initial Synchronization

1. Identify unpaired constructs (Commands without Prompts, or vice versa).
2. Create the missing derived artifacts using the structural mapping rules.
3. Verify semantic equivalence for all pairs.
4. Commit as a single synchronization PR.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#phase-3-ongoing-enforcement]

### Phase 3: Ongoing Enforcement

1. Add parity checks to the CI pipeline (catalog count, name mapping).
2. Require that PRs modifying source constructs include derived updates.
3. Schedule quarterly audits for content drift in instruction files.
4. Add a synchronization step to the construct authoring checklists in [GUID-TECH-IMPL-006](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md) and [GUID-TECH-IMPL-007](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-007-github-copilot-prompt-authoring-guidance.md).
page_texts.26:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#standards-alignment]

### Standards Alignment

- This pattern implements the cross-vendor parity requirement in [STD-TEC-AI-003](../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-003-instruction-file.md) (MR-4).
- Synchronization processes must comply with the construct authoring standards ([STD-TEC-AI-001](../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-001-skill-authoring.md), [STD-TEC-AI-002](../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-002-agent-definition.md)).
page_texts.27:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#governance-integration]

### Governance Integration

- The Technology Domain EA Lead approves source-of-truth designations.
- Parity check failures in CI block merges to the default branch.
- Quarterly synchronization audits are reported to the Architecture Governance Board.
page_texts.29:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#reference-implementation]

### Reference Implementation

Repositories derived from the enterprise bootstrap template demonstrate this pattern:

- Commands in `.claude/commands/` (source of truth)
- Prompts in `.github/prompts/` (derived, with additional Copilot-specific prompts)
- `CLAUDE.md` and `copilot-instructions.md` maintained in semantic parity
- Skills in `.claude/skills/` (shared — same path for both tools)
page_texts.30:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#synchronization-pr-example]

### Synchronization PR Example

A typical synchronization PR modifies paired files:

```
Modified files:
  .claude/commands/pr-appr-review.md          (source — new Command)
  .github/prompts/pr-appr-review.prompt.md  (derived — corresponding Prompt)
```

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

Designate one AI tool's construct catalog as the source of truth, derive the other tool's equivalent through structural mapping, and enforce parity through automated CI checks. This eliminates behavioral drift between Claude Code and GitHub Copilot configurations.
